campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage.measured_by: direct computation over data/k12_modulome/metadata_qc_with_p1k.csv, fetched from the repo (gh CLI to locate, raw download to read) -- NO author contact needed, because the ACCESS WALL is only on log_tpm (the expression matrix), not on the metadata
campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage.comparison: PRECISE-1K alone is 621/1035 = 0.60 glucose over 9 media. Public K-12 is 0.827 glucose among ANNOTATED carbon rows with 42% of rows carrying no carbon annotation at all. The expansion therefore adds mostly MORE GLUCOSE SAMPLES AND UNANNOTATED ROWS -- glucose dominance gets WORSE, not better -- so it does not widen the condition side in the way M2 requires.
campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage.not_apples_to_apples: PRECISE-1K's published bottleneck was an INTERSECTION with Keio's specific 28 carbon conditions; the figure computed here is distinct carbon sources present in the compendium. The two are related but not identical quantities, so the comparison is directional, not exact. The 42%-unannotated and 82.7%-glucose figures stand on their own regardless.
campaign_criterion_M2_condition_coverage.incidental: sucrose appears on 11 samples here, and the sibling Fitness Browser candidate carries a KNOWN bad-sucrose-stock defect on E. coli BW25113 -- any sucrose-based cross-use of the two would inherit it.

candidates.name: The limits of distribution-free conditional predictive inference (Barber, Candes, Ramdas, Tibshirani)
candidates.locator: https://doi.org/10.1093/imaiai/iaaa017  (Information and Inference: A Journal of the IMA 10(2):455-482, 2021; arXiv:1903.04684)
candidates.verification: VERIFIED via search against the published record: full author list, journal, volume, pages, year, DOI and arXiv id all resolved consistently across the OUP page, the arXiv listing and the first author's own publication list.
candidates.claim: Exact conditional coverage is IMPOSSIBLE without assumptions on the underlying distribution. The paper's actual contribution is to map the space between marginal and conditional coverage -- i.e. WHICH RELAXATIONS of conditional coverage remain achievable distribution-free.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: IT EXPLAINS A RESULT WE ALREADY MEASURED AND REFRAMES THE PATH. Our conformal attempt on the inverse cell was 'informative on 0 of 6 splits -- it brackets while proving nothing, since coverage holds even for a useless model'. That is not an implementation gap: it is the price of the guarantee class. And the paper supplies the constructive half -- the achievable relaxations -- so the next move is to PICK AN ACHIEVABLE RELAXATION (or add explicit assumptions), NOT to hunt for a better conformal method. It also names the failure mode that matters to us directly: marginal coverage can cover 99% of one subgroup while badly under-covering another, which is exactly the per-protein heterogeneity our 0.35-0.76 range describes.
blocking_unknowns: Which specific relaxation fits the inverse cell's decision ('propose k, assay k, keep best') is NOT answered by this paper and is the real design question; the paper gives the menu, not our choice.
This CLOSES a line of inquiry (better conformal method) more than it opens one. Valuable, but it narrows rather than unlocks -- do not present it as a lever.

candidates.name: Null/WT-anchored normalisation plus overlapping-variant bridging ('test-equating') as the field's practical cross-assay scale
candidates.locator: UNVERIFIED — synthesised from search summaries of the 2025 Mol Syst Biol DMS variant-scoring review (https://doi.org/10.1038/s44320-025-00137-x) and MaveDB/AVE harmonisation discussion; no primary source fetched
candidates.verification: CORROBORATED 2026-10-09 by an independent first-party search: several sources describe synonymous/nonsense two-point rescaling as the field's working practice. The UNVERIFIED flag is lifted on the PRACTICE; no single primary source was fetched, so the flag stands on the citation.
candidates.claim: Independent corroboration that the scale problem is real and unsolved: 'their scale is highly dependent on experimental methods and selection assays, requiring rescaling and normalisation'. The practical approach is to anchor each assay on shared controls (synonymous/WT and nonsense/null) to a 0-1 range, then rescale across assays via overlapping variants as a bridging set.  CONCRETE RECIPE recovered 2026-10-09: the WT anchor is the paper's own value or the MEDIAN of synonymous variants; where nonsense variants are absent (common), a 'nonsense-like' anchor is the MEDIAN of the worst-1% loss-of-function missense in that dataset. Admission requires >=1 synonymous, >=1 nonsense and >50 missense variants -- which yielded only 103 datasets over 30 proteins from MaveDB, so the anchor requirement is itself a hard filter.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: A null-to-WT-anchored scale would NOT be a physical unit but WOULD be a defensible shared axis ('fraction of the null-to-WT range'), which is more than the inverse cell has now. And it independently confirms our own recorded conclusion that raw calibrators cannot transfer.
blocking_unknowns: ITS FAILURE MODE IN OUR DATA IS ALREADY MEASURED: null-anchoring needs an unsaturated dynamic range, and CcdB is 79.3% tied at its assay ceiling with 8 distinct levels -- the exact degeneracy our own G6 screen excludes it for. So the bridging idea is most likely to fail on the very assay that motivated the problem.
Requires overlapping variants BETWEEN assays; whether TEM-1 and CTX-M-14 share enough is unmeasured.

DYNAMIC-RANGE CLIPPING is the companion caveat, and it is this repo's own assay_degeneracy finding arriving from outside: joint-modelling work truncates scores at a common lower bound because ASSAYS SATURATE AT DIFFERENT POINTS. Any anchoring scheme inherits that.

WORSE FOR OUR PURPOSES: in S. aureus the causal determinants (mecA, blaZ) ARE accessory genes, so a gene-copy-number model may simply be RE-DERIVING A CURATED DETERMINANT CATALOGUE in feature form. The comparator is SNP models, NOT a rule-based determinant caller -- and our own measurement plus Hu et al. 2024 says the rule wins out of distribution. Until re-run with an AMRFinder/ResFinder arm and a per-clade null, it is consistent with 'curated catalogue, laundered through XGBoost'.
Species hazard: oxacillin in S. aureus is this project's own LABEL_CONFOUNDED cell (mecA is an unreliable surrogate; cefoxitin is the CLSI surrogate).

Phenotypes are LABORATORY-MEASURED (per-row laboratory_typing_method; broth dilution dominant); AMRFinderPlus is used for GENOTYPE annotation only, never to infer phenotype. assembly_ID populated on 66.8% of rows (ENA GCA preferred, ERZ fallback, keyed on BioSample). candidates.why_it_could_matter: IT CONTRADICTS THE OPERATIVE PREMISE OF THE AMR TRACK'S CLOSURE. The repo's own strict-MIC 4-drug census (2026-05-18) concluded 'NO drug clears N=150 per-class at either bar', with assembly_accession the structural bottleneck (96% drop on cipro). Run through the repo's OWN tier_for_isolate, CABBAGE clears N=150 per-class at the STRICT bar on four cells: E. coli x ceftriaxone 2,802R/4,212S, Campylobacter x cipro 1,180R/3,532S, E. coli x cipro 509R/5,218S, Salmonella x cipro 196R/21,084S. Salmonella cipro is UNDERPOWERED in the repo at 4-5 R against a bar of 20. It is also not a speculative new source: the EBI AMR Portal already produced this project's first genuinely-INDEPENDENT TB number (39,193-isolate provenance-disjoint cohort), so it has cleared these gates in production once.
blocking_unknowns: G8 IS THE ONE OPEN GATE and it is the expensive one: min_effective_lineages needs genome clustering over the actual assemblies, which must be fetched. 9 of 10 gates pass; this is NOT a pass.

LEAKAGE IS REAL AND MEASURED: 1,011 of the repo's 1,509 manifest accessions (67.0%) appear in CABBAGE -- PATRIC is BV-BRC and NCBI_antibiogram/NDARO are the NCBI-PD family the 10 SCORED cells came from. Manageable rather than fatal: 102,699 CABBAGE assemblies (99.0%) are in NO repo cohort, so the fail-closed cohort_manifest gate costs almost nothing.

G2 IS THE COHORT-WIDE FALLBACK, AND THE SCREEN SAYS SO ITSELF ('weak'). The `database` column is an AGGREGATOR label (semicolon-joined, overlapping: 'NCBI_antibiogram;NDARO'), NOT a BioProject. The repo's source-diversity bar is per-BioProject, so 7 labels at 47% top share is NOT that measurement. BioProject-level diversity is UNMEASURED and needs BioSample->BioProject resolution via ENA.
USELESS FOR THE PROSPECTIVE LOCK: collection_year maxes at 2024 with ZERO rows >=2026, so nothing here is eligible against the active 2026-08-31 cutoff. A clean negative on that forward path.

CENSORING BITES UNEVENLY and the four clearing cells are the good ones: E. coli cipro excludes 51% (CENSORED_EXCLUDED 5,199 -- a <= bound above the S breakpoint), Klebsiella cipro excludes 87% and is S-starved at 32. Campylobacter cipro is the clean one (CENSORED_EXCLUDED exactly 0).
E. coli x gentamicin yields only 67 strict R, so it does NOT serve the open rmt/aac(3) question.

candidates.name: VEFill -- DMS score imputation across protein domains, and the MEASURED within-vs-across-modality limit
candidates.verification: DOI and PMC entry resolve. The performance figures are search-reported and were NOT re-derived from the paper.
candidates.claim: Gradient-boosting imputation of missing DMS scores trained on Human Domainome 1 -- a large STANDARDISED corpus using a UNIFORM stability-based assay -- integrating ESM-1v embeddings, EVE scores, substitution matrices and physicochemical descriptors. R2=0.64 (Pearson r=0.80); generalises reliably to unseen proteins in OTHER STABILITY-BASED datasets but WEAKER on ACTIVITY-BASED assays.
candidates.why_it_could_matter: THIS IS THE DIRECT ANSWER TO F4, and it is a BOUND rather than a lever: cross-assay scale transfer is tractable WITHIN an assay modality and degrades ACROSS modalities. That independently corroborates this project's measured finding that a calibrator could not transfer between TEM-1 and CcdB, and it means the inverse cell's RANK-ONLY deployability MATCHES the field's state of the art rather than falling short of it.
blocking_unknowns: IT IS AN IMPUTATION MODEL, NOT A CALIBRATION-TRANSFER METHOD. It fills missing scores WITHIN a standardised corpus; it does not give an absolute magnitude on a new assay.
CORROBORATION, NOT A PATH: adopting it would not give the inverse cell a dose. The actionable output is the SCOPE RULE (same-modality anchoring only), not the model.
Human Domainome is a human-domain STABILITY corpus; transfer to a bacterial ACTIVITY assay like TEM-1 ampicillin is exactly the across-modality case it measures as weaker.
